front: Displays the TST index/summary in the PNR so you can see TST number, passenger association, total, FOP and segments. Use this before a manual reissue or after ATC confirmed pricing.
Displays TST number 1 in detail. Useful when checking the stored itinerary, fare, taxes, fare calculation, fare basis, baggage, FE/FM/FP/FV and exchange indicators.
Displays the TST associated with passenger 1. Helpful in a multi-passenger PNR when different passengers have different TSTs.
Displays TST information associated with segments 4–5. Segment association is especially important in partial reissues.
Displays the historical pricing record, including who priced it, when it was priced, and how it was priced (system vs. manual).
Creates a blank TST for all passengers and segments. Used as a starting point for 100% manual pricing/reissues.
Creates a blank TST specifically for segments 4, 5, and 6. Use when manually pricing only part of the itinerary.
Creates a blank TST specifically for passenger 1. Use when doing a manual reissue for only one person in a party.
Creates a blank TST specifying the passenger type code as Adult (ADT). Important for forcing adult taxes/fares in a manual TST.
Modifies passenger association in an existing TST. Assigns TST 1 to passenger 1. Critical when splitting TSTs in multi-passenger reissues.
Removes the TST index from the PNR completely. Use this if you made a mistake and need to start the manual pricing over.
Removes only TST number 1. Useful if there are multiple TSTs and only one is incorrect.
Updates the fare basis in the TST (for segment 2) to Y26. Required when manually building a TST to match the old or new fare rule.
Sets the "Not Valid Before" (NVB) date on segment 2 to 10 December. Used to match ticketing restrictions.
Sets the "Not Valid After" (NVA) date on segment 2 to 10 December. Often tied to maximum stay rules.
Updates the free baggage allowance on segment 2 to 2 pieces (2PC). Essential for preserving baggage rights on a manual reissue.
Enters the base fare amount in USD (450.00). Must match the base fare being charged for the new journey.
Enters the base fare amount in GBP (450.00). Ensure currency matches the point of origin or desired currency.
Enters the final total amount for the ticket (825.00 USD). This is Base Fare + Taxes + Penalty (if collected as tax).
Adds a specific tax to the TST (25.00 USD, code US). Represents a new tax being collected or an old tax being carried forward.
Marks the passenger as exempt from the specified tax code (US). Used for specific passenger types (e.g., diplomats) or routing rules.
Adds multiple taxes simultaneously. Adds a 25.00 USD 'US' tax and a 10.00 USD 'AY' tax.
Removes the specific tax code (US) from the TST. Use this if a tax was incorrectly added or is no longer applicable on the new routing.
Overwrites ALL existing taxes with new ones. The 'T' indicates these are the only taxes. Replaces the old tax list.
Enters the Equivalent Fare Paid (350.00 GBP). Used when the base fare currency differs from the ticketing currency.
Enters the Banker's Selling Rate (1.250). Used alongside the Equivalent Fare to define the exchange rate used for conversion.
Enters the Rate of Exchange (0.850000). Used when converting NUCs (Neutral Units of Construction) to the local base currency.
Adds free text to the Endorsement box (FE). Often used to indicate restrictions like "NONREF/REBOOK 50USD PENALTY".
Adds a Tour Code to the FT box. Used for corporate fares, IT/BT fares, or agency-specific discount codes required by the airline.
Adds the Form of Payment to the FP box. Crucial for ticketing.
Specifies the FOP for a reissue. 'O/' indicates the old FOP (e.g., CASH) and '+/CH' adds the new FOP (e.g., CHQ) for any additional collection.
Enters the Original Issue details (FO line). Requires Document Number, Date (DDMMM), City, IATA. Absolutely mandatory for any reissue.
Enters the complete fare calculation line (FC). Shows how the fare was constructed (city pairs, NUCs, Roe, etc.). Must accurately reflect the journey.
back: FC LON BA NYC 500.00 BA LON 500.00 NUC1000.00END ROE1.00

front: Forces the Validating Carrier (FV) to British Airways (BA). Essential when interlining or if the system defaults to the wrong airline.
Initiates the Amadeus Ticket Changer (ATC) process to automatically calculate fare differences, taxes, and penalties for a changed itinerary.
Runs ATC re-pricing against a specific historical TST (TST 1). Useful if the PNR has multiple TSTs or a complex history.
Runs ATC re-pricing for Passenger 1 only. Used when only one passenger in a multi-pax PNR is changing their flights.
Runs ATC re-pricing focusing on specific segments (4 and 5). Helps ATC understand which segments are being exchanged.
Forces ATC to use a specific ticket number for the exchange calculation. Crucial when the automatic FO line retrieval fails or is ambiguous.
Forces ATC to attempt pricing even if it encounters minor errors. Similar to 'best buy' pricing but for reissues. Use with caution.
Runs a "what-if" ATC calculation without saving the TST. Use this to quote a penalty/fare difference to a customer before they confirm.
Displays the detailed breakdown of the ATC calculation (Base, Tax, Penalty, Total Add Collect/Refund). Review this carefully before confirming the reissue.
Issues the ticket based on the stored TST. The standard command used after a successful manual TST build or ATC confirmation.
Issues the ticket specifically from TST 1. Use when multiple TSTs exist in the PNR to avoid issuing the wrong one.
Issues the ticket specifically for Passenger 1. Used in multi-passenger reissues where pax are ticketed separately.
Issues the ticket and applies the Form of Payment (CASH) at the time of ticketing. Overrides or provides the FOP if missing from the TST.
Issues the ticket and sends the output to a designated printer. Used for hardcopy receipts/itineraries.
Voids ticket number 1 in the PNR. Must be done on the same day of issuance (usually before midnight local time). Irreversible.
Displays the electronic ticket record. Always check the ticket status (OPEN, FLOWN, EXCH, RFND) before attempting a reissue or refund.
Initiates an automated refund calculation. The system tries to calculate the refund amount based on fare rules.
Initiates an automated refund calculation for a specific ticket number.
Manually updates the Total Refund Amount to 200.00. Used during manual refunds or to correct an automated refund calculation.
Manually updates the refundable tax amount for code US to 15.00. Used to adjust tax refunds.
Adds or updates a cancellation penalty of 50.00. This amount is deducted from the refund total.
Finalizes and processes the refund transaction. This commits the refund to the reporting system (BSP/ARC).
Ignores and cancels the refund process. Use if you started a refund but realized it was a mistake before finalizing.
Displays the history of the electronic ticket. Shows changes in status (e.g., OPEN to EXCH to FLOWN) and timestamps.
Requests standard flight availability from LHR to JFK on 10NOV.
Requests availability from LHR to JFK on 10NOV, specifically on British Airways (BA).
Requests availability from LHR to JFK on 10NOV, looking for flights departing around 09:00 AM.
Requests direct access availability into a specific carrier's system. Often more accurate than standard availability.
Displays the timetable (scheduled flights, not necessarily available seats) from LHR to JFK on 10NOV.
Sells 1 seat in Y class from line 2 of the availability display.
Sells 2 seats in M class from line 3 of the availability display.
Waitlists 1 seat in J class from line 4. The status code returned will be LL instead of HK.
Sells 1 seat in Y class on line 1, and the corresponding connecting flight on the next line.
Sells a seat without an availability display. Requires Carrier (BA), Flight Number, Class, Date, Origin/Destination, and Number of Seats.
Cancels itinerary segment number 2.
Cancels itinerary segments 2, 3, and 4.
Cancels all itinerary segments in the PNR. Passenger details remain.
Sells 1 seat in Y class from line 1 and inserts it into the itinerary after existing segment 2. Useful for keeping flights in chronological order.
Manually changes the status code of segment 2 to HK (Holding Confirmed).
Attempts to change the booking class of segment 2 to 'M' class. Only works if 'M' class is available on the same flight.
Prices the itinerary at the lowest available fare for the currently booked classes.
Prices the itinerary and attempts to rebook into the lowest available class, even if it requires changing the current booking class.
Prices the itinerary for Passenger 1 only.
Prices the itinerary using only segments 2 and 3.
Prices the itinerary forcing the Passenger Type Code to Child (CHD).
Prices the itinerary but does not create a TST. Used to quote a price to a customer without saving it.
Finds the lowest available fare and rebooks the classes informatively (does not save changes to PNR).
Displays the fare rules for the fare basis priced in TST 1. Essential for checking cancellation and change penalties.
Displays Category 16 (Penalties) for the fare rule associated with TST 1. Saves reading the entire rule text.
Displays a list of available fares (Fare Quote Display) from LHR to JFK on 10NOV for carrier BA.
Displays fares from LHR to JFK on 10NOV, specifically for 'Y' class.
Adds one adult passenger named SMITH/JOHN MR.
Adds one child passenger named SMITH/TOM MSTR, specifying they are a child (CHD) and their date of birth.
Adds one adult passenger and an infant on lap. The infant's name and DOB must be included in the INF brackets.
Modifies passenger name number 1. (Note: Many airlines prohibit name changes; this is often restricted to minor corrections).
Deletes passenger number 1.
Adds the agency contact phone number.
Adds the passenger's home phone number.
Adds the passenger's mobile phone number.
Adds an email address to the PNR. Important for e-ticket receipts and schedule change notifications.
Sets a ticketing time limit (TL) indicating the ticket must be issued by 10NOV.
Updates the ticketing element to indicate the ticket has been issued (OK).
Adds the "Received From" field (RF). Mandatory before saving any changes to a PNR.
Ends the transaction, saves the PNR, and immediately retrieves it back to the screen.
Ends the transaction and saves the PNR. The screen clears.
Ignores unsaved changes and clears the screen.
Adds an Other Service Information (OSI) message for all airlines (YY) indicating the passenger is a VIP.
Adds an OSI message specifically directed to British Airways (BA).
Requests a Wheelchair to/from the gate (WCHR) for passenger 1. SSRs require airline action/confirmation.
Requests a Vegetarian Vegan Meal (VGML) for passenger 1.
Adds a Frequent Flyer number for passenger 1 on British Airways (BA).
Adds a general remark (RM) to the PNR. Visible only to the agency, not sent to the airline.
Adds a remark (RIR) that will print on the passenger's itinerary document.
Initiates the split/divide process by separating Passenger 1 into a new PNR.
Files the new (child) PNR created during the divide process. Must be followed by finishing the original (parent) PNR.
Retrieves a PNR using its 6-character alphanumeric Record Locator (e.g., ABCD12).
Retrieves a list of PNRs matching the surname SMITH.
Displays the complete history of changes made to the PNR, including who made them and when.
Moves the display down to view more information.
Moves the display up to view previous information.
Moves the display to the very bottom of the output.
Moves the display to the very top of the output.
Finds the 3-letter IATA city code for London.
Finds the city name for the 3-letter IATA code LHR.
Finds the 2-letter IATA airline code for British Airways.
Finds the airline name for the 2-letter IATA code BA.
Finds the 3-letter IATA equipment code for a Boeing 777.
Finds the aircraft type for the 3-letter IATA code 777.
Calculates the Great Circle distance (mileage) between London (LHR) and New York (JFK).
Converts 100 USD to GBP using the current system exchange rate.
Displays the current system date and time.
Calculates the date 30 days after 10NOV.
Displays the count of PNRs in all queues for the current office.
Starts working through Queue 1, Category 0. Displays the first PNR in that queue.
Removes the current PNR from the queue and displays the next one.
Leaves the current PNR on the queue (doesn't remove it) and displays the next one.
Exits the queue processing mode.
Places the current PNR onto Queue 5, Category 0 for the designated office ID.
Signs into the Amadeus system. Requires user ID and password prompts to follow.
Signs out of the Amadeus system.
Displays the current Office ID (OID) you are signed into.
Routes hardcopy tickets (ATB) to printer ID 123456.
Routes itinerary documents (IEP) to printer ID 654321.
Opens the main Help menu in Amadeus.
Opens the Help page specifically for the TQT command.
Enters Secure Flight Passenger Data (SFPD) Date of Birth for passenger 1 (Format: DDMMMYY). Mandatory for US flights.
Enters SFPD Gender for passenger 1 (M or F).
Enters Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) passport details including country, number, nationality, DOB, gender, expiry, and name.
Forces an update to the free baggage allowance to 1 Piece on a manual TST for segment 2.
Creates a blank Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) record. Used for collecting miscellaneous fees (e.g., penalty fees not collected as a tax).
Displays the EMD summary/index in the PNR.
Issues the EMD based on the stored TMC record.
Displays a specific tariff record.
Shows detailed information for a specific flight, such as meal service, equipment, and on-time performance.
Checks the Minimum Connecting Time (MCT) allowed between flights at a specific airport (e.g., LHR).
Revalidates an e-ticket to match a new flight/date without requiring a full reissue (rarely used now, depends on airline policy).
Takes ownership of a PNR created by an airline or another agency, provided security permissions allow it.
Views the agency's stored profile information.
Moves data from a stored corporate profile into the current PNR.
Checks the check-digit and basic validity of a ticket number format.
Adds mandatory security information required by certain governments.
Views the history of changes made only to the itinerary segments.
Displays real-time operational status (arrived, delayed, departed) of a flight for the current day (FLIFO).
Displays the seat map for segment 2.
Requests specific seat 14A for the passenger on segment 2.
Requests any Aisle (A) seat for the passenger on segment 2.
Cancels the assigned seat on segment 2.
Sends a plain text itinerary to the default itinerary printer or email.
Generates an agency invoice for the booking.
Modifies a name to reflect a marriage change, requiring specific airline format and authorization.
Shows the commission percentage or amount stored in the TST.
Manually updates the commission to 5% on the TST.
Views the net fare calculation if a negotiated or private fare is used.
Adds a remark indicating a net fare was used, often required for accounting.
Sends a message or the PNR directly to an airline's specific queue.
Sends a Teletype (TTY) free-text message to an airline regarding a PNR.
Shows interline ticketing agreements between airlines.
Shows standard baggage allowances and fees for a specific airline/route.
Quotes only the taxes for an itinerary, without the base fare.
Forces a specific ticketing date (past or future) for manual calculation purposes.
Adds an infant to an existing adult passenger record without a seat.
Requests UNMR service and provides necessary contact details for an unaccompanied minor.
Shows a summary of all Special Service Requests present in the PNR.
Removes a specific SSR (e.g., meal request) from the PNR by element number.
Restricts fare quote to only show corporate or negotiated rates.
Attaches a corporate discount code to the pricing command.
Retrieves the PNR quickly without loading the extensive history file.
Immediately dispatches the itinerary to the stored email address.
Views default settings (currency, language) for the specific office ID.
Safely closes the session and disconnects from the terminal emulator.
